The key laws and regulations governing PFM in Uzbekistan, ordered from highest to lowest authority, are:

1. Constitution of the Republic of Uzbekistan – Highest legal authority, referenced in the Budget Code and foundational for all legislation.
2. Budget Code of the Republic of Uzbekistan – Organic budget law adopted in 2013, primary framework for the budget system and process.
3. Annual Law on the State Budget – Enacted each year by Parliament, sets appropriations and fiscal rules for the year.
4. Presidential Decrees – Issued to supplement budget laws and adjust fiscal parameters; have force of law.
5. Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers – Secondary legislation implementing Budget Code provisions and budget execution.
6. Orders and Normative Acts of the Ministry of Economy and Finance – Include technical instructions, budget classification, and treasury regulations.
7. Instructions on Budget Classification – Lower-tier regulation specifying application of budget classification.
8. Treasury Circulars and Budget Circulars – Operational guidance for budget preparation and execution.
9. International Treaties – Supersede national law where applicable, as per the Budget System Law.
10. Earlier Law on the Budget System – Predecessor to the Budget Code, referenced for continuity provisions but largely superseded.

This hierarchy is directly evidenced in Uzbekistan's official legal database and the Budget Code, with additional detail from PEFA and official government sources. The Tax Code and Central Bank regulations, while relevant to fiscal management, are not directly evidenced as core PFM laws in the retrieved material and are therefore omitted.
